analysis.title: Up and Adam
key_insights: The PHLX Semiconductor Index (SOX) fell 6.7% in one day, its steepest daily decline since June, on concerns about AI financing. Over the past 12 trading days it has trailed the S&P 500 by 17%, the second-widest margin in 20 years.

Historically, when the SOX has trailed the S&P 500 by 10% or more on a rolling 12-day basis, it has outperformed the S&P by an average of 5% over the next three months. The firm cites oversold technicals (14-day RSI below 30), P/E multiples at a discount to the S&P 500 and expected solid hyperscaler earnings, and remains optimistic on semis.

Workers with employer-sponsored family health coverage contribute an average of $7,471 toward premiums in 2026, up 9% YoY versus 7.6% last year (KFF survey). The increase is more than twice the pace of wage growth. More hikes may come in 2027 as Medicaid spending cuts take effect.

Consumer spending looks resilient. Synchrony and Capital One reported YoY credit card spending growth of 8% and 11%, with stable delinquencies and lower charge-offs. Initial jobless claims were below 200k for the sixth straight week.

The Pentagon signed a contract to buy 850 F-35s over the next ten years. Long-term contract visibility lets manufacturing capacity scale with demand. Sustained US and allied defense spending is a key reason the firm favors the Industrials sector.

The 10-year Treasury yield fell 17 bps to 4.96%, its first close below 5% in a month and the steepest one-day decline since August 2024, while WTI rose 1.9%. Treasury yields have become less tethered to oil. The AI-related share rout and renewed Middle East hostilities drove a flight to safety, with short-covering in Treasury futures amplifying the move.

S&P 500 closed at 7,663 (-1.2% on the day, +11.9% YTD) and the Nasdaq 100 at 28,959 (-2.9% on the day, +14.7% YTD). The Russell 2000 rose 0.1% to 2,784 and the DJIA was flat at 52,868. The USD Index was 101.61.

sector_views.rationale: The firm remains optimistic on semis after the SOX selloff, citing oversold technicals, a P/E discount to the S&P 500 and expected solid hyperscaler earnings.
Sustained growth in US and allied defense spending, including the 850 F-35 purchase contract, supports the sector.

earnings_insights: Synchrony Financial and Capital One reported 3Q YoY credit card spending growth of 8% and 11% respectively, with stable delinquency rates and lower charge-offs (reported).
Large banks' 3Q earnings calls last week gave a constructive view on consumer spending.
Hyperscaler earnings are expected to be solid (forecast, per the firm).
